text: The complaint-to-contact match is the match branch of the one published deviation-outcome operation, PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} (API-S8-002) on /api/recovery/deviation/v1 with case-record right U, taking a DeviationOutcome and answering a Deviation; the operation, the element names, the right and the status codes are copied from TSD S8 T-A.1 and T-A.2, each error condition is bound to one message of the legacy set, no second path is declared, and the match's own property names are settled in the baseline review.
why: TSD S8 T-A.1 publishes two operations for the module and the legacy story names exactly those two endpoints; no source publishes an operation for a complaint-to-contact match. Declaring a third path, or leaving the element names to the builder, would invent an interface the sources do not have, and the legacy criteria say the officer acts on the screen and the system writes the result.
read: TSD S8 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T3.1; API Specification v4 paths /cases/{caseId}/deviations and /deviations/{deviationId} and elements Deviation, DeviationRequest and DeviationOutcome; FSD S8 A2.18.2; legacy RWB-E7-009 Endpoints; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13 and R5.4 class H
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7009-APP sections 1, 4, 7, 12.1 and 13; RWB-S8-E7009-CON sections 2, 3, 7 AC1, 8 BR12, 12.1 and 15
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-deviation tech lead, before the contract is tagged
impact: Both stories build the match behind the published operation, and a build that adds a second path fails the contract review

text: The complaint reference, the contact reference and the match outcome are request inputs of the match branch that are recorded in the local decision record, and no column of deviation carries them; the baseline fixes them as optional additive properties of the DeviationOutcome request with a placeholder name, format and value set until the business lead confirms them, and a repeat is matched on the deviation and complaint references because the operation declares no Idempotency-Key.
why: TSD S8 T3.1 gives deviation ten columns and none is a complaint or a contact reference, the FSD field catalog of A2.18.3.2 lists the same eight fields, the API Specification v4 declares no such property, and TSD S8 T3.2 publishes no list for them. Adding a column, a field ID or an enumeration would be a business value, and dropping the references would leave the match with nothing to bind.
read: TSD S8 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2; FSD S8 A2.18.3.1 and A2.18.3.2; API Specification v4 Deviation and DeviationOutcome; legacy RWB-E7-009 AC1, AC2 and Data; Template and Rules v1 R9
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7009-APP sections 3, 4, 8 BR1, 8 BR8, 11, 13 and 15; RWB-S8-E7009-CON sections 7 AC2, 8 BR7, 11 and 12.1
confirm: Business lead and the rwb-deviation tech lead, before wave 4 starts
impact: The match is recorded on the ledger with two references and an outcome, no column and no migration is added, and a later reference-data list can arrive as an additive change

text: The preceding contact is read from rwb-source-data on a REST consumed row, because the S8 row of the connection matrix names REST and events to P1 and nothing to EFS, and the interaction ledger is rwb-source-data's by the default ruling; the FSD's EFS integration point is reached only through P1 and never by a direct client from this service.
why: FSD S8 A2.18.2 names EFS as an integration point, but the connection matrix gives S8 no EFS edge and the target forbids ACE and outside reads from a route service; the default ruling gives the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data. Reading EFS directly would add an edge the architecture does not have, and reading an ACE table or a v_ace_* view would break DP-05.

text: This step publishes no event: EV-06 DeviationRaised and EV-07 DeviationCleared belong to the raise and clearance steps of the stage, the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is recorded as a missing H row, and rwb-reporting's S8 subscription therefore carries no match fact, so the conduct measure rests on the decision-record ledger.

DP-09 is absent from the pattern set of this key, and rwb-reporting listens to S8 on the connection matrix, which makes the missing projection a tracked gap rather than a build item.

text: The match is authorised on the case-record right U: the Conduct and QA officer (RW-CONDUCT) is the primary role the FSD names and needs U to record, although TSD S8 T6.1 gives it R only, so the permission table and the right of the published operation are taken over the matrix row and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved by giving the role a new right.
why: FSD S8 A2.18.3.3 names 'Conduct and QA officer' as primary, the legacy permission table gives the case record right U, TSD S8 T-A.1 declares right U on both operations, and TSD S8 T6.1 gives RW-CONDUCT R. Taking the matrix row alone would leave the feature with no role that can record it, and granting a new right would invent an access row.
